$comment: Restaurant identity and contact details. No field here is provisional any more. The last one that was is seo.url, which held Astro’s example.com and so put that domain in the canonical tag of every page on the site — see CLAUDE.md for how that went unnoticed. npm run check flags any $comment containing the marker word (upper-case, the one this sentence is deliberately not spelling), so use it again if a field goes back to being provisional. What is still genuinely open is noted where it applies: address.$comment asks for a native-speaker check on the Greek spellings. See README, Before launch.
name: fokia
$comment-phone: Two numbers. `phone` is the landline and is the site's primary number: it answers reservations and take away during service, it is what the server renders on every card, and it is what the JSON-LD advertises. `phoneAfterHours` is the mobile, for calls made once the restaurant has shut. The Take away band holds four dialling controls, and a clock-driven swap evaluated against `hours` below in Europe/Athens rewrites three of them to the mobile outside service — the reservations panel and both service cards. The take away panel never swaps, because take away only runs during service. NB this comment has been wrong before: for one revision both numbers were shown at once under 'during hours' / 'after hours' labels and the swap was deleted as dead code, then the cards became buttons and it came straight back. If you edit the swap, edit this line. Editing either number here changes it everywhere.

address.$comment: Confirmed by the client. `street` and `city` are locale-keyed so the Greek page is not left reading a Latin transliteration of a Greek street name. VERIFY the Greek spellings before launch.

geo.$comment: Supplied directly by the client. Feeds the `geo` block in the JSON-LD, which is omitted entirely if either is null. These sit 1.3m from the marker coordinates inside `mapUrl` — the two are not meant to match to the metre and neither is wrong: mapUrl is Google's own link to the listing and carries Google's marker, while these are the client's own reading. Do not 'reconcile' them by editing the URL.

$comment-mapUrl: Google's documented Maps URLs form (https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/urls/get-started#map-action), addressing the listing by its Place ID. Deliberately NOT the long /maps/place/... URL the browser produces: everything after data= in one of those is length-prefixed — !4m6 declares 'six tokens follow', !3m5 declares 'five' — so dropping a token that looks redundant leaves the counts short and Google silently degrades the link to a name search on the wrong pin, with nothing erroring anywhere. That shipped once. This form has no such structure and nothing safe-looking to delete. The placeId below is the same listing: its base64 decodes to the two 64-bit ids 0x14a1af007ee38927 and 0x9619f033941949e, which are exactly the pair in the !1s field of the client's original share URL. Feeds both the button in FindUs and `hasMap` in the Restaurant JSON-LD.
$comment-mapUrl-provenance: The Place ID inside mapUrl came from the client via Google's Place ID finder, alongside their share link https://maps.app.goo.gl/yBC9YH1GG524MJPWA for the same listing. Neither is stored as a field of its own — the Place ID is already in mapUrl and the share link is not rendered anywhere, and an unused key here is how directionsUrl came to sit in this file unnoticed for months.

hours.$comment: Confirmed by the client. `days` uses schema.org day names for the JSON-LD. List EVERY day an entry covers, not just the first and last: FindUs.astro computes contiguous runs from this, so a gap in the list correctly becomes two rows instead of one range claiming a day the restaurant is shut. `closed` is empty because the restaurant now opens seven days — keep the key rather than deleting it: FindUs.astro and the JSON-LD both read it, and a closed day may come back.

$socialComment: Order here is the order shown in the nav and the footer. `id` selects the icon in components/SocialLinks.astro — an id with no matching icon is skipped, so add the icon before adding the network.

seo.$comment: `url` is the production domain, confirmed by the client. It is the only place the domain is written: canonical URLs, og:url, the sitemap and robots.txt all derive from it. `ogImage` is the share card under public/, regenerated by `npm run og` — a path, not a URL, because Base.astro resolves it against `url` and social crawlers reject a relative one.
